streamCheck.title: Model Health Check
streamCheck.message:
Health check tests provider connectivity by sending a direct API request. The following may cause check failures:

• Official providers (uses OAuth login, no standalone API Key)
• Some relay services (verify requests come from Claude Code CLI)
• AWS Bedrock (uses IAM signature authentication)

A failed check does not mean the provider is unusable — it only means it cannot be verified via a standalone request. Please refer to actual behavior within the application.

commonConfig.title: About Common Config
commonConfig.message:
The "Common Config Snippet" lets you share plugins, environment variables, and other settings across different providers so they won't be lost when you switch.

How to use:
① Edit a provider and click "Edit Common Config" → "Extract from Editor"
② When creating a new provider, check "Write Common Config" (enabled by default)

If you've newly installed plugins or hooks, re-extract the common config to keep them in sync.

codexQuotaProtection.title: Official quota protection
codexQuotaProtection.help: Pause new official requests when either usage threshold is reached; third-party models remain available. Covers Codex official requests through CC Switch local routing only. Usage is read from the quota information official responses already carry, so normal use adds no extra requests; only the first request, or one after about 5 idle minutes, triggers a separate quota lookup. When usage can't be determined (network problems, expired login, and so on) requests go through as usual instead of being blocked. Requests already admitted and other apps can still push usage past a threshold; while paused, ordinary-quota exhaustion won't activate Luna Reserve.
codexQuotaProtection.hint: Pause at either cutoff. Defaults: 95% / 98%. Saved changes apply to new requests immediately.

codexConfig.reasoningModeHint: Enable when the upstream Chat Completions API supports toggling thinking on/off. Providers like Kimi, GLM and Qwen usually fall into this category.

codexConfig.subagentModelNotInCatalog: This model is not in the model list: Codex can't get its context window, and when routing converts requests to Chat / Anthropic it is replaced by the default model.
codexConfig.agentMaxThreadsHint: How many sub-agents (not counting the main agent) one Codex session can run at the same time. This is a Codex-wide setting written to [agents] max_threads in config.toml, and it stays the same when you switch providers. Leave empty for the Codex default: 6 with the classic sub-agent tools, 3 with the new ones. Codex has no unlimited option and the minimum is 1; more sub-agents use up quota faster. Takes effect after reopening Codex.

agentTooltip.sisyphus: Main orchestrator responsible for task planning, delegation and parallel execution. Uses extended thinking (32k budget) and drives workflows through TODO lists to ensure task completion.
agentTooltip.atlas: Main orchestrator (holds TODO list) responsible for task distribution and coordination during execution phase. Delegates to specialized agents rather than completing all work directly.
agentTooltip.prometheus: Strategic planner that collects requirements through interview mode and creates detailed work plans. Can only read/write Markdown files in .sisyphus/ directory, never writes code directly.
agentTooltip.hephaestus: Autonomous deep worker ("legitimate craftsman") inspired by AmpCode deep mode. Goal-oriented execution that launches 2-5 explore/librarian agents in parallel for research before taking action.
agentTooltip.oracle: Architecture decision and debugging advisor. Read-only consulting agent providing excellent logical reasoning and deep analysis. Cannot write files or delegate tasks.
agentTooltip.librarian: Multi-repository analysis and documentation retrieval expert. Deeply understands codebases and provides evidence-based answers. Excels at finding official documentation and open-source implementation examples.
agentTooltip.explore: Fast codebase exploration and context grep expert. Uses lightweight models for high-speed search. The scout for understanding code structure.
agentTooltip.multimodalLooker: Visual content expert that analyzes PDFs, images, charts and other non-text media, extracting information and insights from them.
agentTooltip.metis: Plan consultant that performs pre-analysis before planning. Identifies hidden intents, ambiguities and AI failure points to prevent over-engineering.
agentTooltip.momus: Plan reviewer that validates plan clarity, verifiability and completeness with high precision. Rejects and requests revisions until plans are perfect.
agentTooltip.sisyphusJunior: Category-generated executor, automatically created via category parameters. Focuses on executing assigned tasks and cannot re-delegate, preventing infinite delegation loops.

categoryTooltip.visualEngineering: Frontend and visual engineering category for UI/UX design, styling, animation and interface implementation. Defaults to Gemini 3 Pro model.
categoryTooltip.ultrabrain: Deep logical reasoning category for complex architectural decisions requiring extensive analysis. Defaults to GPT-5.3 Codex ultra-high reasoning variant.
categoryTooltip.deep: Deep autonomous problem-solving category with goal-oriented execution. Conducts thorough research before action, suitable for difficult problems requiring deep understanding.
categoryTooltip.artistry: Highly creative and artistic task category that inspires novel ideas and creative solutions. Defaults to Gemini 3 Pro max variant.
categoryTooltip.quick: Lightweight task category for single-file modifications, typo fixes, and simple adjustments. Defaults to Claude Haiku 4.5 fast model.
categoryTooltip.unspecifiedLow: Uncategorized low-effort task category for tasks that don't fit other categories with small workload. Defaults to Claude Sonnet 4.5.
categoryTooltip.unspecifiedHigh: Uncategorized high-effort task category for tasks that don't fit other categories with large workload. Defaults to Claude Opus 4.6 max variant.
categoryTooltip.writing: Writing category for documentation, prose and technical writing. Defaults to Gemini 3 Flash fast generation model.

slimAgentTooltip.orchestrator: Writes executable code, orchestrates multi-agent workflow, summons experts

reason.defaultWhileRouting: While routing, the default is the provider you route to. You can pick another one when switching to Aggregation.
reason.directDefaultCannotDelete: Leaving routing switches back to this provider, so it can't be deleted. On the direct page, choose "Back to direct and use" on another provider first.
reason.noFailover: Official accounts can't join the failover queue: they use the client's own login and can't rotate with other providers.

dialog.routeLead: Requests go through CC Switch on this machine first, then to the provider you pick.
dialog.stackLead: The default provider takes requests without a prefix.
dialog.stackOfficialNote: If you use an official subscription, set the official account as the default provider.
dialog.routeNoteFile: Rewrites the address and key in {{file}}. The real key stays in CC Switch; other settings are untouched.
dialog.routeNoteSwitch: Changing providers later on the Routing tab won't rewrite the config file.
dialog.routeNoteKeepRunning: Keep CC Switch running. Quitting writes the direct config back; it reconnects on the next start.
dialog.desktopRouteNoteModels: Claude Desktop's model list becomes the routed provider's models; switching the routed provider later rewrites the config file.
dialog.desktopRouteNoteRestart: {{app}} only reads its config at launch: restart {{app}} after confirming.
dialog.desktopRouteNoteKeepRunning: Keep CC Switch running so {{app}}'s requests can go out.
dialog.stackNoteMembers: {{names}} add {{count}} models, shown in /model with the ccs- prefix.

dialog.stackNoteEmpty: No other providers added yet, so only the default is available. You can add more on the Aggregation tab later.
dialog.stackNoteNoFailover: Aggregation has no failover. The queue and its settings are kept and come back with routing.
dialog.stackNoteRestartCodex: Restart {{app}} to see the aggregated models; quit the desktop app completely and reopen it.
dialog.leaveStackNote: The ccs- aggregated models disappear from /model. The aggregation list is kept and they come back when you switch to aggregation again. If you're using one of them, pick a regular model in /model.

dialog.exitLead: {{app}} will connect to {{provider}} directly; requests no longer go through CC Switch.
dialog.exitNoteFile: Rewrites the address and key in {{file}} back to {{provider}}'s; other settings are untouched.
dialog.exitNoteRouteKept: The routing target, failover queue and settings are kept and come back the next time you start routing.
dialog.desktopExitNoteRouteKept: The routing target is kept and comes back the next time you start routing.
dialog.needsRouteLead: {{provider}}: {{reason}}. If you switch to it directly, {{app}} won't be able to use it.

help.title: How the connection modes differ
help.direct: Direct: CC Switch never touches your requests; the client talks to the chosen provider itself for the most native experience.
help.route: Routing: requests go through CC Switch on this machine, unlocking hot-switching providers, failover, format conversion, and other advanced features.
help.stack: Aggregation: models from several providers sit together in /model, so you can switch between them seamlessly inside the client.
